facts.fact: The Federal Government has revived the national digital postcode project, fully federally funded for the first time, to give every standing building a unique GIS-enabled location identifier, and NIMC and NIPOST signed an MoU to integrate postcode retrieval into the NIN platform, which users will 'soon' be able to use (NIPOST Postmaster General and NIMC Director-General).
NIMC's Director-General says the NIMC Act 2026 positions the commission as the root certification authority for the national public key infrastructure.

NGA.note: The document says nothing on links between civil registration and the ID system.

facts.fact: NIMC's Director-General refers to the 'newly enacted NIMC Act 2026', which strengthens the commission's enforcement powers and modernises the legal framework for digital identity.

NGA.note: Only a passing mention of a digital transformation agenda; no strategy is described.
No enrolment count or share is given.
Nothing on a number given at birth.
Nothing on who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the NIN is described.
No statement on the ID system's issuance, biometrics or certification.
Address verification via the NIN is only planned ('soon'); no other system is stated to check people against the ID.
